title: [dogfood:P0] Default SQLite connection pool wedges the whole server on the documented env-var install (begin tx deadline exceeded -> API bricked until restart)
detail: Reproduced twice on fresh build at 8e3e7e6, 2026-09-09. Starting the server the README env-var way (CONSENSUS_DB_URL=sqlite:///... CONSENSUS_PORT=8124 ./consensus serve, no config file): the FIRST goal-driven session wedges the entire server. Sequence: 'harness: found active session' -> 'planning: starting interactive session' -> exactly 3m later 'harness: planning failed ... error="planning: initial context: read context: begin tx: sqlite: begin tx: context deadline exceeded"' -> heartbeat auto-retries the same session forever. During the wedged window the API first returns 401 UNAUTHENTICATED to the valid admin key, then stops answering entirely (no-auth /api/v1/health times out, HTTP 000). kill -9 -> integrity ok -> restart -> heartbeat resumes the poisoned session -> re-wedges within seconds: a session wedged this way bricks the instance on every boot (only fix is deleting the session/DB). A/B PROOF it is the pool: identical run with config-file database: { max_open_conns: 4 } executes the full loop cleanly (llm: calling provider -> response received -> commands staged -> committing -> idle). The env-var path exposes no max_open_conns override and the WAL grew to 1.5MB on a near-idle DB = pool starvation signature. Fix direction: (1) pin a safe default sqlite pool (max_open_conns<=4 or equivalent) instead of unlimited; (2) put harness transactions on a separate pool/connection class from API reads; (3) stop heartbeat-resume on a session that failed N consecutive planning windows (poison-pill guard); (4) fail loud: 'begin tx deadline' should surface as a 5xx/health-degraded event, not a silent server freeze. Evidence: /tmp/dogfood-consensus/server.log + server2.log (wedged) vs server3.log (clean), same binary.
